test_title: PYST 62: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Why are micro-nutrients important for plants?

options.text: They increase the size of the plant roots.
They help in the absorption of sunlight.
They are only needed for decorative plants.
They support essential functions even in small amounts.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They support essential functions even in small amounts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Micronutrients**, often referred to as **trace elements**, are essential dietary elements required by plants in very small quantities, typically less than **10 mmole per kg** of **dry matter**.
 
• These nutrients are vital because they act as **cofactors** for **enzymes** and participate in essential **redox reactions** and **metabolic processes** within the plant cells.
 
• Statement 1 suggests they primarily increase the size of plant roots. While certain nutrients influence root architecture, this is not the defining characteristic of micronutrients as a group. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2 claims they help in the absorption of sunlight. Sunlight absorption is the primary role of **Chlorophyll**, which contains **Magnesium** (a macronutrient); micronutrients like **Iron** only assist in its synthesis. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 3 posits they are only for decorative plants. In reality, all plants, including **agricultural crops**, **forest trees**, and **aquatic plants**, require them for survival. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 4 states they support essential functions even in small amounts. This is the fundamental definition of micronutrients, as their absence leads to **deficiency symptoms** and prevents the plant from completing its **life cycle**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The **eight** essential micronutrients include **Iron (Fe)**, **Manganese (Mn)**, **Copper (Cu)**, **Molybdenum (Mo)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Boron (B)**, **Chlorine (Cl)**, and **Nickel (Ni)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Nutrients:**
 
 
• **Macronutrients:** These are required in large amounts (exceeding **10 mmole per kg** of dry matter). Examples include **Nitrogen (N)**, **Phosphorus (P)**, **Potassium (K)**, **Calcium (Ca)**, **Magnesium (Mg)**, and **Sulphur (S)**.
 
• **Micronutrients:** Required in minute quantities, often measured in **parts per million (ppm)** or **micrograms**.
 
 
 
• **Specific Functions of Micronutrients:**
 
 
• **Zinc (Zn):** Essential for the synthesis of **Auxin** (a plant hormone) and activates various **carboxylases**.
 
• **Boron (B):** Necessary for **pollen germination**, **cell elongation**, and **translocation of carbohydrates**.
 
• **Molybdenum (Mo):** A component of **Nitrogenase** and **Nitrate reductase**, enzymes involved in **nitrogen metabolism**.
 
• **Iron (Fe):** Required in larger amounts than other micronutrients; it is a constituent of **Ferredoxin** and **Cytochromes**.
 
 
 
• **Criteria for Essentiality:** Proposed by **Arnon and Stout** in **1939**, stating an element is essential if the plant cannot complete its **life cycle** without it and the element is directly involved in **plant metabolism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Toxicity vs. Deficiency:** There is a narrow range of concentration at which micronutrients are optimum. Any slight decrease causes **deficiency**, while a slight increase can cause **toxicity**.
 
• **Manganese Toxicity:** An excess of **Manganese** can induce deficiencies of **Iron**, **Magnesium**, and **Calcium** by competing for uptake or binding sites.
 
• **Beneficial Elements:** Apart from the **17 essential elements**, some plants require **Sodium (Na)**, **Silicon (Si)**, **Cobalt (Co)**, and **Selenium (Se)** for specific functional needs.
 
• **Mobility:** Elements like **Nitrogen** and **Potassium** are highly **mobile**, so deficiency symptoms appear first in **older leaves**. In contrast, **Calcium** and **Iron** are **immobile**, and symptoms appear first in **younger leaves**.
</ul
